tools.name: create_comments
tools.description: Add comments, questions, or replies to a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Anyone who can read it may comment and reply. Set parentCommentId to reply to a top-level comment. To mention people, get their userId and displayName from list_mention_candidates, write @<displayName> in the body, and list their userIds in mentionUserIds (clientMutationId is then required). Items are applied in order and each one commits on its own; results report each item (ok, or status and error).

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

items.description: Comments to add, applied in order

body.description: Comment text (plain text, 1..10000 characters). To mention someone, include @<displayName> exactly as returned by mcp__ainecto__list_mention_candidates.

kind.description: COMMENT (default) or QUESTION. A reply (parentCommentId) is always COMMENT. A QUESTION can later be resolved with mcp__ainecto__resolve_comments.

parentCommentId.description: Reply to this top-level comment id (from mcp__ainecto__list_comments). Replies are one level deep: replying to a reply is rejected. The thread's original author and earlier repliers get a notification email (except people mentioned in this reply, who get the mention email instead).

mentionUserIds.description: userIds to mention (from mcp__ainecto__list_mention_candidates). Each one's @<displayName> must appear in body; newly mentioned people get a notification email.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Required when mentionUserIds is not empty; reuse the same value when retrying the same item so the mention email is not sent twice.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the comment notification email (mention or reply). Defaults to en.

tools.name: delete_comments
tools.description: Delete your own comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Only the author can delete. A resolved question and a top-level comment that still has replies cannot be deleted. Each id is applied on its own; results report each id.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List the active comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid), oldest first, including replies (a reply has parentCommentId set; replies are one level deep). Each comment has id, kind (COMMENT or QUESTION), body, author, mentions (userId, label and position in the body), and for questions questionState (UNANSWERED, ANSWERED, RESOLVED) and resolvedAt. Anyone who can read it can list its comments.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

tools.name: list_mention_candidates
tools.description: List the people you can mention in comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid): userId, displayName and jobTitle (null = not set) — jobTitle helps tell people with the same name apart. Only people who can read it are listed — for a card, the people who can read its board, which are also the people a card can be assigned to. To mention someone, write @<displayName> exactly in the comment body and pass their userId in mentionUserIds of create_comments or update_comments. Page with nextCursor while hasMore is true.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

query.description: Name filter, 0..100 characters. Omit or leave empty for the first page of everyone.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page (same parent and query).

tools.name: resolve_comments
tools.description: Mark questions on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid) as resolved. Only top-level comments with kind QUESTION can be resolved, and it needs edit access to the document or board (readers can comment but cannot resolve). Resolving cannot be undone. Each id is applied on its own; results report each id.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

ids.description: Question ids to resolve (top-level comments with kind QUESTION)

tools.name: update_comments
tools.description: Edit your own comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Only the author can edit, and only while they can still read it. A resolved question and a top-level comment that already has replies are locked. Items are applied in order and each one commits on its own; results report each item.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

body.description: New comment text (replaces the old text).

mentionUserIds.description: The complete set of userIds mentioned after the edit; omit to remove all mentions. Each one's @<displayName> must appear in body. Only people who were not mentioned before get a notification email.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Required when mentionUserIds is not empty; reuse the same value when retrying the same item so the mention email is not sent twice.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the comment notification email (mention or reply). Defaults to en.

tools.name: diagram_apply_changes
tools.description: Required single-call mutation path for diagram node/edge/group create/update/delete changes. Put nodes, edges, and groups in one request and call this once. Do not look for type-specific diagram CUD tools; this tool is the only diagram CUD entry point.

uuid.description: Required for update/delete; optional for create

text.description: Node text/label. Supports newlines (\n) for multi-line display.

groupUuid.description: Group UUID; empty string clears membership

uuid.description: Required for update/delete

bridgeType.description: Omit (null) for a plain node-to-node edge. Set only when a group is an endpoint: GROUP_TO_GROUP|NODE_TO_GROUP|GROUP_TO_NODE

uuid.description: Required for update/delete

width.description: Explicit width; omit to keep it derived from member nodes

height.description: Explicit height; omit to keep it derived from member nodes

uuid.description: LLM request UUID

inputTokens.description: Provider total input tokens; Java persists uncached input after one normalization

cachedInputTokens.description: Cached subset of provider total input tokens

creditsCharged.description: Deprecated; ignored. Credits are calculated server-side from tokens.

uuid.description: LLM request UUID

status.description: Target status — currently only FAILED is mutable from caller side

tools.name: erd_arrange_tables
tools.description: Arrange ERD tables after edits. Default incremental mode places newly-created tables while preserving existing positions; full=true re-layouts the entire diagram. Use after several separate table edits to tidy the canvas.

full.description: Re-layout the ENTIRE diagram (overwrites existing positions). Default false = arrange only newly-added (uncoordinated) tables to the top-right while preserving existing table positions. Call this after creating several tables to tidy them up.

tools.name: erd_apply_changes
tools.description:
Required single-call mutation path for ERD create/update/delete changes. Put tables, columns, indexes, refs, enums, enum_values, and table groups in one operations array and call this once.
Rules: (1) all data field names are snake_case; (2) for create, generate your own UUIDs and put them in data.uuid, then later operations in the same batch may reference those UUIDs without read-back calls; (3) enum values are separate enum_value operations, not inline on enum; (4) ref.relationship uses short dbdiagram-style symbols: >, <, or -; (5) ref_column operations map FK columns explicitly, never automatically.
Do not look for type-specific ERD CUD tools; this tool is the only ERD CUD entry point. If operations is very large, use request_upload_token with purpose=mcp.call and send the tools/call payload with curl to save LLM tokens.
One-call worked example:
{
  "documentUuid": "erd-doc-uuid",
  "description": "create users/posts ERD",
  "operations": [
    {"op":"create","type":"table","data":{"uuid":"tbl_users","name":"users","display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_users_id","table_uuid":"tbl_users","name":"id","type":"bigint","is_pk":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_users_email","table_uuid":"tbl_users","name":"email","type":"varchar(255)","is_unique":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"table","data":{"uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"posts","display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_id","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"id","type":"bigint","is_pk":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_author_id","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"author_id","type":"bigint","is_not_null":true,"display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_status","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"status","type":"post_status","is_not_null":true,"display_order":3}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status","name":"post_status"}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum_value","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status_draft","enum_uuid":"enum_post_status","value":"draft","display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum_value","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status_published","enum_uuid":"enum_post_status","value":"published","display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"ref","data":{"uuid":"ref_posts_author","name":"fk_posts_author","from_table_uuid":"tbl_posts","to_table_uuid":"tbl_users","relationship":">","on_delete":"cascade"}},
    {"op":"create","type":"ref_column","data":{"uuid":"refcol_posts_author","ref_uuid":"ref_posts_author","from_column_uuid":"col_posts_author_id","to_column_uuid":"col_users_id","display_order":1}}
  ]
}

arrangeNewTables.description: Whether to auto-place newly-created tables after the batch; defaults to true

tools.name: erd_get_table
tools.description: Get one ERD table with nested columns and indexes. Returns persistent table/column/index UUIDs usable directly as erd_apply_changes update/delete targets and ref_column column references. Column fields use apply_changes snake_case names: uuid, table_uuid, name, type, is_pk, is_unique, is_not_null, is_increment, default_value, note, display_order. Index fields include uuid, name, columns (column UUIDs), is_unique, is_pk, type.

tableUuid.description: Table UUID. Response includes columns[] and indexes[] with persistent UUIDs for apply_changes.

inputSchema.description: Get one ERD table with nested columns and indexes. Returns persistent table/column/index UUIDs usable directly as mcp__ainecto__erd_apply_changes update/delete targets and ref_column column references. Column fields use apply_changes snake_case names: uuid, table_uuid, name, type, is_pk, is_unique, is_not_null, is_increment, default_value, note, display_order. Index fields include uuid, name, columns (column UUIDs), is_unique, is_pk, type.

tools.name: get_my_work_summary
tools.description: One-call summary of what is waiting for the signed-in user in AiNecto — call it when the user asks things like "do I have anything to do?", "anything new?", "anything to review?" or "did anyone ask me something?". Returns notifications {unread (not yet read by the person — the same read state as the web bell, so reading on the web lowers it at once; newest 100 counted; unreadCapped when there are more; the same number as the line at the end of tool results), unreadByKind}, mentionsToRead {items the person has not read that mention them, each with target title and url}, and todos {open (stays until the to-do is done or closed; the to-dos on that line), leaseExpired, inProgress, items: questions and requests waiting for the user's agent} and cards {kanban cards assigned to the user on boards they can read now: assignedOpen, pendingAcceptance (assigned but not yet accepted or declined), inProgress, inReview, blocked, items: the first page}. For details use list_notifications, list_agent_todos and kanban_list_cards; to read the document and its comments use get_document with the target uuid. Read-only: nothing is marked read or acknowledged.

workspaceUuids.description: Only items in any of these workspaces.

projectUuids.description: Only items in any of these projects. Use it when the user names a project or the project you are working in is clear. With workspaceUuids too, both must match. A workspace or project you cannot see matches nothing.

tools.name: list_agent_todos
tools.description: List the to-dos that ask the signed-in user's agent to act now (for example a question that mentions the user). This is the current state, not a feed: a to-do you have not finished comes back on every call until it is completed, dismissed, or closed because the person did it themselves. Each item has todoId, kind, obligation, openedAt, summary, target (title and url), action and state. To work on one, claim it with update_agent_todos and complete it with a one-line note. Actions that affect other people (assigning, approving, inviting) need the user's confirmation first.

state.description: OPEN (default): to-dos you can take, including ones whose lease expired. MINE: to-dos currently leased (claimed) and not expired.

workspaceUuids.description: Only to-dos in any of these workspaces.

projectUuids.description: Only to-dos in any of these projects. Use it when the user names a project or the project you are working in is clear. With workspaceUuids too, both must match. A workspace or project you cannot see matches nothing.

after.description: todoId of the last item of the previous page.

tools.name: list_history
tools.description: List recent activity (who did what, people and agents) in a workspace, a project, or on one resource, newest first. Give at least one of workspaceUuid, projectUuid, or resourceType with resourceUuid; you need editor access or higher in that scope. This is a list to refresh, not a gap-free feed: to see what is new, read the first page again and skip ids you have already seen; to get each new notification exactly once use list_notifications. Each item has id, kind, at, lastAt, coalesceCount, actor, target (title and url only when you can read it now), changes and summary.

resourceType.description: With resourceUuid: activity on one resource.

resourceUuid.description: UUID of the resource named by resourceType.

before.description: nextCursor of the previous page (older items).

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: Read new notifications for the signed-in user, oldest first and without gaps — for an agent that checks the inbox periodically. The server remembers, per connection and per filter (kinds, workspaceUuids, projectUuids, directOnly), how far you have acknowledged; a new filter starts from now. Each response carries ackToken: pass it as ack in your next call (with the same filter) after you have handled the batch — if you do not, the next call returns the same batch again (identify duplicates by id and seq; an item that comes back with a higher seq and a larger groupCount is an update of the same entry). Each item has id, seq, kind, at, summary (one line), actor, target (title and url only when you can read it now), action (what the user is asked to do) and humanRead. An item you can no longer read comes back as {id, seq, at, redacted: true}. This tool never marks anything read for the person (use mark_notifications_read when the user asks); open to-dos are in list_agent_todos. Calls closer than 30 seconds apart (except a call that carries ack) return retryAfterSeconds instead of items.

cursor.description: Where to read from. "saved" (default): after what this connection last acknowledged for this same filter. "latest": from now on (moves the saved position to now). "earliest": everything still kept (90 days). Or a nextCursor from a previous response: read after it without using or changing the saved position.

ack.description: The ackToken of the previous response. Send it with the same filter once you have handled (or safely stored) that batch; only then does the saved position move past it. Without it, the same batch is returned again.

workspaceUuids.description: Only notifications in any of these workspaces.

projectUuids.description: Only notifications in any of these projects. Use it when the user names a project or the project you are working in is clear. With workspaceUuids too, both must match. A workspace or project you cannot see matches nothing.

directOnly.description: Only notifications that point at you directly (mentions, questions to you).

tools.name: mark_notifications_read
tools.description: Mark the signed-in user's notifications as read in the AiNecto inbox — the same read state as the web bell, so the unread badge goes down. Call it only when the user explicitly asks you to mark notifications read; reading or acknowledging notifications (list_notifications ack) does not do this. Pass the id and seq of each item as you received them. Results are per item: {id, ok: true, readAt, alreadyRead?} or {id, ok: false, error} with error one of STALE (the entry was updated after you saw it — it stays unread; seq is the current one), NOT_FOUND (not your notification, archived, or no such id), INVALID. unread is the user's unread count after the call (the number on the web bell, unreadCapped when above it). Only your own notifications. Retrying is safe. It does not close to-dos and does not acknowledge anything for list_notifications.

items.description: Notifications to mark read; each item is applied and reported on its own.

id.description: Notification id from list_notifications or get_my_work_summary (mentionsToRead).

seq.description: The seq of that same item as you received it. If the entry was updated after you saw it (higher seq), it stays unread and you get STALE.

tools.name: update_agent_todos
tools.description: Claim, renew, complete, release, or dismiss the signed-in user's agent to-dos. Only the session holding the current leaseToken may renew, release, or complete a claimed to-do — even another session of the same connection gets CLAIMED_BY_OTHER. Results are per item: {todoId, ok: true, state, leaseToken?, claimExpiresAt?} or {todoId, ok: false, error} with error one of CLAIMED_BY_OTHER, LEASE_LOST, ALREADY_DONE, CLOSED_BY_HUMAN, SUPERSEDED, ACCESS_LOST, BUSINESS_ACTION_REQUIRED, NOT_FOUND, INVALID — on CLOSED_BY_HUMAN or SUPERSEDED stop working on it. BUSINESS_ACTION_REQUIRED: card to-dos (CARD_*) cannot be completed here; doing the card action closes them. Retrying the same complete or dismiss returns ok again. To mark the person's notifications read (only when they ask), use mark_notifications_read.

items.description: To-dos to update; each item is applied and reported on its own.

action.description: claim: take it (returns leaseToken, valid 30 minutes). renew: extend your lease. complete: done (with leaseToken if you claimed it; without one only while it is still OPEN). release: give it back. dismiss: not a to-do.

leaseToken.description: Required for renew and release, and for complete or dismiss of a to-do you claimed.

note.description: For complete or dismiss: one line on what you did (at most 500 characters, no document bodies). The person sees it in the inbox.

tools.name: kanban_apply_changes
tools.description: Create, edit, reorder and link cards on one kanban board in a single atomic call (at most 100 operations; if one fails nothing is applied and the error carries operationIndex and code). Creating and editing cards needs edit access to the board; move with toBoardUuid moves a card to another board of the same project. The assignee may also check acceptance criteria and add result links (DELIVERABLE, REVIEW_RESULT, TEST_EVIDENCE). create also sets assignee, requester, reviewers and watchers in the same call. To change a card's column, reassign it, accept, approve, block, watch and similar, use kanban_card_action. Results list each operation's card uuid, revision, status and sortKey.

operations.description: Operations, applied in order in one transaction. If any fails, none is applied and the error names operationIndex.

op.description: create: a new card in To Do (you become its requester unless requesterUserId names someone else). update: change only the fields you send (send null to clear description, dueAt). move: reorder within the card's column, or with toBoardUuid move it to another board of the same project. link / unlink: attach or remove a document or an external URL.

cardUuid.description: Target card (update, move, link, unlink). It must be on this board. From kanban_list_cards — by cardKeys if you only have the card key, e.g. KAN-15.

description.description: Markdown description. Keep it short — link longer text as a document instead. update: null clears it.

dueAt.description: Due time, ISO-8601 instant such as 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z. update: null clears it.

criteria.description: Acceptance criteria. update replaces the whole list; the assignee may only flip done.

assigneeUserId.description: create only: assign the new card (userId from list_mention_candidates with the board's documentUuid). Someone other than you gets an assignment to accept. To reassign an existing card use kanban_card_action assign.

requesterUserId.description: create only: the requester (reporter) instead of you; they are notified. To change it later use kanban_card_action set_requester.

reviewerIds.description: Reviewers (userIds from list_mention_candidates with cardUuid or the board's documentUuid). update replaces the whole list.

watcherIds.description: Watchers who get activity notifications. update replaces the whole list.

responderIds.description: update only: who should answer while the card is blocked.

linkRole.description: Link role. The assignee may add DELIVERABLE, REVIEW_RESULT and TEST_EVIDENCE links; other roles need edit access to the board.

documentUuid.description: AiNecto document to link (you must be able to read it). Give this or url.

url.description: External http(s) URL to link, e.g. a pull request. Give this or documentUuid.

label.description: Optional label for an external URL.

linkRole.description: Link role. The assignee may add DELIVERABLE, REVIEW_RESULT and TEST_EVIDENCE links; other roles need edit access to the board.

documentUuid.description: AiNecto document to link (you must be able to read it). Give this or url.

url.description: External http(s) URL to link, e.g. a pull request. Give this or documentUuid.

label.description: Optional label for an external URL.

linkId.description: unlink: the linkId from the card's links.

afterCardUuid.description: Place after this card in the column (create, move).

beforeCardUuid.description: move: place before this card in the column.

toBoardUuid.description: move: another kanban board (document UUID) in the same project to move the card to. It keeps its key, column, people, comments, links and to-dos; afterCardUuid / beforeCardUuid then name cards on that board. Needs edit access to both boards, and everyone on the card (requester, assignee, reviewers, watchers, responders) must be able to read the new board.

clientMutationId.description: create: idempotency key — retrying with the same value returns the same card instead of creating another.

expectedRevision.description: The card revision you last read. If the card changed since, the whole call fails with CARD_CHANGED and the current card. Send it when people may edit the card too.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the emails these operations may send (review requests to newly named reviewers). Defaults to en.

tools.name: kanban_card_action
tools.description: Do one workflow action on a kanban card, the same as the buttons in the web app. ★Before assign (to someone other than the signed-in user), approve or quick_done, show the user what will happen and get their explicit confirmation — these change other people's work and notify them. Actions: assign / unassign; accept / decline (only the assignee — accepting closes the assignment to-do); start (To Do → In Progress; anyone who can edit the board, or the assignee — not while an assignment is waiting to be accepted); request_review (→ In Review); approve (→ Done) / request_changes (→ In Progress) by the requester or a reviewer; quick_done (To Do → Done); reopen (Done → In Progress); block / unblock; archive / unarchive; set_requester; watch / unwatch (yourself). Doing the action is what closes the matching card to-dos — update_agent_todos cannot complete them. Returns the card after the action (status, assignment state, allowedActions) and reasonCommentId when a reason was saved.

cardUuid.description: Card UUID (from kanban_list_cards — by cardKeys if you only have the card key, e.g. KAN-15).

action.description: The action. Which ones you may do now is the card's allowedActions in kanban_list_cards (with cardUuids).

reason.description: Saved as a comment on the card. Required when the action's allowedActions entry says reasonRequired (e.g. decline, reopen).

assigneeUserId.description: assign: who gets the card — someone who can read the board (list_mention_candidates with cardUuid). Your own userId assigns it to you and accepts at once.

responderIds.description: block: who should answer (people who can read the board). Omit to keep the card's current responders.

expectedRevision.description: The card revision you last read. If the card changed since, the call fails with CARD_CHANGED and the current card. Send it when people may act on the card too.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the email this action may send (assignment or review request). Defaults to en.

tools.name: kanban_list_cards
tools.description: Read kanban cards. Three ways: cardUuids (or cardKeys) → those cards in full, including allowedActions (what you may do now with kanban_card_action) and links; boardUuid → the board's columns To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done (each with hasMore and nextAfter); none of these → cards across all boards you can read where you are the assignee (or requester / watcher), most recently updated first. Each card has uuid and key (KAN-15 — the short id people use in chat; find a card by it with cardKeys, then use its uuid in the write tools), title, status, assignee and assignmentState (PENDING = not yet accepted), blocked, revision and allowedTransitions.

boardUuid.description: Board (document) UUID: list its columns, first page each (or one column with status).

cardUuids.description: Read these cards in full (description, people, links, allowedActions). Use alone.

cardKeys.description: Read these cards in full by their key (e.g. KAN-15 — the short id people use in chat), the same as cardUuids. Use alone.

relation.description: Without boardUuid: cards across boards where you are the assignee (default), the requester or a watcher.

includeDone.description: Without boardUuid: also recently completed cards.

projectUuid.description: Without boardUuid: only boards in this project.

cursor.description: Next page: nextCursor (without boardUuid) or a column's nextAfter (with boardUuid and status).

limit.description: Cards per page (per column with boardUuid). Default 20.

tools.name: markdown_append_document
tools.description: Append to Markdown documents. If the appended body is tens of KB or more, prefer request_upload_token (purpose=document.append) and upload the body with curl.

uuid.description: Document UUID

addition.description: Body addition. 추가할 내용이 크면 (수십 KB 이상) LLM 토큰 절약을 위해 `request_upload_token (purpose=document.append, scopeJson={documentUuid, separator})` 로 uploadUrl 을 받고 curl 로 PUT 으로 보낼 것.

separator.description: Separator between existing body and addition

tools.name: create_documents
tools.description: Create documents. projectUuid comes from list_projects (a workspace UUID is not a project UUID). Set shareEnabled to also turn on each document's public link and get its shareUrl in the same call. If a document body is tens of KB or more, prefer request_upload_token (purpose=document.create) and upload the body with curl.

type.description: Document type. Creatable values: erd, diagram, markdown, openapi, html, file, kanban.

typePayload.description: Type-specific payload for enabled document types. markdown: {body}; diagram: {diagramSource,sourceLanguage,edgeStyle,isModule,metadata}; openapi: {content}; html: {content} (a full HTML page); file: no JSON payload — bytes go through request_upload_token(purpose=document.create, scopeJson={projectUuid,folderUuid?,type:"file",title,filename}) then one curl PUT (images·PDF·mp4/webm·audio·text/code·CSV only); kanban: no payload — creates an empty board; add cards with kanban_apply_changes.

body.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for typePayload.body when document type is markdown. 본문이 수십 KB 이상으로 크면 LLM 토큰 절약을 위해 `request_upload_token (purpose=document.create)` 를 호출해 uploadUrl 을 받고 curl 로 직접 PUT 으로 보낼 것.

shareEnabled.description: Optional. true turns on the document's public link right after creating it, exactly as enable_shares does (needs the right to manage sharing; types without a public page are refused). The created item then carries shareUrl, the page anyone can open. If sharing is refused, this item is not created.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace UUID — null uses user's default workspace

targetType.description: Share target type. A document gets a shareUrl anyone can open; a project gets a public API path only (there is no public project page); a folder token is stored but nothing public reads it yet.

uuid.description: Attachment UUID

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read a document. The body comes back for the types whose create/update take one: markdown → content; openapi → content (the spec text) + format/specVersion/pathCount/operationCount; html → content (the HTML text); file → file {filename, contentType, sizeBytes, viewerKind} + content for text/CSV (first 64 KB); diagram → diagramSource/sourceLanguage/edgeStyle/isModule/metadata; kanban → board {viewer, columns: each column's first 20 cards + hasMore} (more cards and card details via kanban_list_cards); erd → metadata only (read tables/refs via erd_list_*).

uuid.description: Document UUID
Project UUID
Workspace UUID

type.description: Optional document type filter. Readable values: erd, diagram, markdown, openapi, html, file, kanban.

q.description: Optional full-text query. When provided, results come from the search index instead of folder listing.

limit.description: Result cap when q is set (default 50)
Result cap when q is set (default 50)

uuid.description: Document UUID

newFolderUuid.description: New folder UUID — null/empty for root

targetProjectUuid.description: Target project UUID — omit to stay in current project

targetWorkspaceUuid.description: Guard only: must match targetProjectUuid workspace

clientMutationId.description: Optional mutation identifier for client retry tracing

uuid.description: Folder UUID

newParentFolderUuid.description: New parent UUID — null/empty for root

uuid.description: Project UUID

targetWorkspaceUuid.description: Destination workspace UUID (you need write access there)

tools.name: request_upload_token
tools.description: Use this for large payloads of tens of KB or more to save LLM tokens. purpose=mcp.call returns a short-lived bearer token that can call any MCP tool, including erd_apply_changes, via curl. purpose=document.create/update/append uploads document bodies directly to the upload endpoint with PUT/curl. Tokens are reusable for 5 minutes by default.

purpose.description: Token 용도. `mcp.call` 은 curl 로 /mcp 호출, `document.create/update/append` 는 PUT body 로 본문 업로드, `attachment.upload` 는 파일 bytes 업로드. 콘텐츠가 크면 (수십 KB 이상) LLM 토큰 절약을 위해 이 도구로 5분 재사용 토큰을 받고 curl 로 보내는 것을 강력 권장.

scopeJson.description: 선택 — JSON scope. document.create 는 projectUuid, type, title 을 포함하고 creatable type values 는 erd, diagram, markdown, openapi, html, file, kanban. document.update/document.append 는 documentUuid 를 포함. type=file 은 filename 도 포함(확장자로 형식 판정) — PUT 의 Content-Type 은 파일 MIME, 본문은 파일 바이트. attachment.upload: {documentUuid, filename}; storageKey 는 서버가 발급 scope 에 넣는다.

tools.name: update_documents
tools.description: Update documents. If a replacement body is tens of KB or more, prefer request_upload_token (purpose=document.update) and upload the body with curl.

uuid.description: Document UUID

typePayload.description: Type-specific payload for enabled document types. markdown: {body}; diagram: {diagramSource,sourceLanguage,edgeStyle,isModule,metadata}; openapi: {content}; html: {content} (a full HTML page); file: {file:{filename,contentType,sizeBytes,viewerKind}} (+content for text/CSV, first 64 KB); kanban: no body — only the title can be updated; cards are changed with kanban_apply_changes and kanban_card_action.

body.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for typePayload.body when document type is markdown. 본문이 수십 KB 이상으로 크면 LLM 토큰 절약을 위해 `request_upload_token (purpose=document.update)` 를 호출해 uploadUrl 을 받고 curl 로 직접 PUT 으로 보낼 것.

uuid.description: Folder UUID
Project UUID
Workspace UUID

storageKey.description: Storage key returned by request_upload_token purpose=attachment.upload

type.description: Optional document type filter. Readable values: erd, diagram, markdown, openapi, html, file, kanban.

tools.name: identity_get_self
tools.description: Return the authenticated MCP caller identity summary: userId, display name, and job profile (the user's job title and areas — personal context only, it never changes what they may do). Never returns email or token claims.

tools.name: identity_list_job_roles
tools.description: List the job roles the signed-in user can pick for their own job profile — the same list as the account settings screen: roles {code, title, family}, families, areas {code, title}, suggested role codes, customCode (pick it to type a title that is not in the list) and titleMaxLength. Use the codes with identity_update_job_profile. A job profile is personal context only; it never changes what the user may do.

tools.name: identity_update_job_profile
tools.description: Set the signed-in user's own job profile (job role and areas) — the same setting as the account settings screen. It only ever changes the caller's own profile. Pick code and areas from identity_list_job_roles; pass null as code to clear it. Returns the saved jobProfile in the same shape as identity_get_self (null when cleared). Invalid values fail with INVALID_JOB_PROFILE and change nothing. A job profile is personal context only; it never changes what the user may do.

code.description: Job role code from identity_list_job_roles, or its customCode to type your own title. null clears the job profile.

title.description: The role title in the user's own words — required with the custom code, ignored for a listed role (its title comes from the list).

areas.description: Area codes from identity_list_job_roles; the first is the primary area. At least one with the custom code, optional for a listed role. Each area once.
